newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate leaps on late liquidity squeeze.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate leaps on late liquidity squeeze.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed up a sharp 370 basis points to 23.50 percent on Wednesday.
Dealers said a big player held on to liquidity until shortly before the close and pushed up rates with a large trade of 300 million pesos, to take advantage of demand for cash.
Wednesday saw the deadline for banks to settle balances outstanding on checking accounts they hold with the central bank, traders said.
"There was heavy speculation at the close over the cutoff, and that was it," a trader said.
Dealers said they expected rates to fall on Thursday, once demand for liquidity eased and following mild inflation figures released in late trade.
Banco de Mexico announced in late dealing the Consumer Price Index had risen by 0.89 percent on June, or just below an average forecast increase of 0.90 percent in a Reuters survey.
"They'll wipe the slate clean, everything points towards rates going back down. The peso is strong and inflation is under control," the trader added.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts closed 1.65 centavos firmer at 7.8840/7.8860 per dollar.
Banco de Mexico drained 1.165 billion pesos from the market by placing three direct Cetes sales and two repos.

Overnight rates on bank paper closed up 100 basis points at 21 percent, but still far below government paper, which dealers said was most unusual and a sign of how anomalous the late spike in government rates was.
Liquidity of 1.115 billion pesos was scheduled to return to the system from prior central bank participation.
